stem: The student wants to emphasize the significance of the wool fragment. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 2019, conservators at a regional museum in Norway examined a wool fragment found inside a farmhouse wall.
• The fragment measures 14 by 9 centimeters and is dyed a deep blue.
• Dye analysis showed that the blue came from indigo, a plant grown in South Asia.
• Previously, the oldest indigo-dyed cloth known from the region dated to the 1600s.
• The fragment dates to about 1350, nearly three centuries earlier.
choices: Found inside a Norwegian farmhouse wall, the wool fragment measures 14 by 9 centimeters and is dyed a deep blue.
Dating to about 1350, the indigo-dyed fragment is nearly three centuries older than any such cloth previously known from the region.
Conservators found that the fragment's deep blue dye came from indigo, a plant that was grown in Norway at the time.
The indigo-dyed wool fragment that conservators examined at the museum in 2019 has been dated to about 1350.
explanation: The goal asks why the fragment matters. The notes build to the last two bullets: the fragment is nearly three centuries older than any indigo-dyed cloth previously known from the region. Choice B gives the date together with that comparison, and the comparison is what makes the fragment significant.

A.why: You picked an accurate description of where the fragment was found, how big it is, and what color it is. None of that says why the fragment matters, so it doesn't do what the goal asks.

C.why: The notes say indigo was grown in South Asia, not Norway. This choice misstates where the dye plant came from, and it still doesn't explain why the fragment is significant.

D.why: You chose the bare date. 'About 1350' only matters next to the earlier record of the 1600s, and this choice leaves that comparison out, so the significance never comes through.

stem: The student wants to emphasize the significance of Lind's survey. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 1987, economist Teodora Lind published a survey of 2,400 seasonal farmworkers in Sweden.
• Lind recorded the hours each worker put in per week, including time spent traveling between farms.
• Earlier wage surveys had counted only the hours workers spent on the job site.
• By including travel time, Lind showed that the workers' true hourly pay was about 20 percent lower than official figures suggested.
choices: In 1987, economist Teodora Lind published the results of a survey of 2,400 seasonal farmworkers in Sweden.
Lind's survey showed that seasonal farmworkers' true hourly pay was about 20 percent higher than official figures suggested.
Lind recorded the weekly hours of seasonal farmworkers, including the time they spent traveling between farms.
By counting travel time that earlier surveys ignored, Lind showed that true hourly pay was about 20 percent below official figures.
explanation: To show significance, you need what the survey revealed and why that was new. Choice D gives both: Lind counted travel time that earlier surveys had left out, and doing so showed that workers' real pay was about 20 percent lower than the official figures.

A.why: This choice tells you who ran the survey, when, and how many workers it covered. It never says what the survey showed or why it mattered, which is what the goal asks for.

B.why: The notes say true pay was about 20 percent lower than official figures, not higher. This choice reverses the finding.

C.why: You picked the method. Describing what Lind recorded doesn't say what that showed, and it doesn't mention that earlier surveys left travel time out, so the significance is missing.

stem: The student wants to emphasize the significance of the grinding stone found at Tell Qaran. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Tell Qaran is an archaeological site in present-day Jordan.
• In 2016, a team led by archaeologist Samir Haddad excavated a grinding stone at the site.
• Residue on the stone contained starch from wild barley.
• The residue dates to about 12,000 years ago.
• That is roughly 1,500 years before barley is known to have been farmed in the region.
choices: Residue on the Tell Qaran stone shows that people were grinding barley about 1,500 years before it is known to have been farmed there.
In 2016, a team led by archaeologist Samir Haddad excavated a grinding stone at Tell Qaran, a site in present-day Jordan.
The grinding stone excavated at Tell Qaran carries residue of wild barley starch that dates to about 12,000 years ago.
The grinding stone from Tell Qaran proves that people in the region began farming barley about 12,000 years ago.
explanation: The last note explains why the find matters: the residue is about 1,500 years older than the earliest known barley farming in the region. Choice A states that comparison directly, so it makes clear why the stone is significant.

B.why: This choice says who found the stone, when, and where. That information is accurate, but it doesn't explain why the find is important.

C.why: You chose the bare date. '12,000 years ago' only becomes significant when it's compared with when barley farming began, and this choice leaves that comparison out.

D.why: The starch came from wild barley, and the notes say farming came about 1,500 years later. Claiming that the stone proves farming began 12,000 years ago goes beyond the evidence.

stem: The student wants to emphasize the achievement of Ferrán's bridge design. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Velmora Bridge spans a 410-meter river gorge in northern Chile.
• Engineer Lucía Ferrán designed the bridge in 1931.
• It is built from a series of reinforced concrete arches.
• The region has had four major earthquakes since the bridge opened.
• Of the region's bridges from the 1930s, the Velmora Bridge is the only one to have survived all four undamaged.
choices: Ferrán's Velmora Bridge is built from a series of reinforced concrete arches and spans a gorge in northern Chile.
Designed by engineer Lucía Ferrán in 1931, the Velmora Bridge spans a 410-meter river gorge in northern Chile.
Ferrán's Velmora Bridge is the only 1930s bridge in the region to have come through four major earthquakes undamaged.
Like the region's other bridges from the 1930s, Ferrán's Velmora Bridge has survived four major earthquakes undamaged.
explanation: An achievement needs to be measured against something. Choice C says the Velmora Bridge is the only bridge of its era in the region that survived all four earthquakes undamaged, and being the only one is what makes the design an achievement.

A.why: You picked a description of what the bridge is made of and where it is. That says what the bridge looks like, not what it accomplished.

B.why: This choice says who designed the bridge, when, and how long a gorge it crosses. None of that shows why the design was an achievement.

D.why: The notes say the Velmora Bridge was the only 1930s bridge to survive undamaged. Saying it did 'like' the others reverses that and erases the very thing that makes it an achievement.

stem: The student wants to emphasize the significance of the Kora-7 variety. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Cassava is a staple root crop in parts of West Africa.
• In 2014, plant breeder Amaka Eze developed a cassava variety called Kora-7.
• Kora-7 has broad leaves and pale yellow roots.
• Mosaic disease and brown streak disease are the two viruses that cause the greatest cassava crop losses.
• In field trials, Kora-7 became the first cassava variety to resist both.
choices: Developed by plant breeder Amaka Eze in 2014, Kora-7 is a variety of cassava, a staple root crop in parts of West Africa.
Kora-7 became the first cassava variety to resist both of the viruses that cause the greatest losses of the crop.
Kora-7 is a cassava variety, developed by plant breeder Amaka Eze, that has broad leaves and pale yellow roots.
Because it resists mosaic and brown streak disease, Kora-7 has ended cassava crop losses across West Africa.
explanation: The note that explains why Kora-7 matters is the last one: it was the first variety to resist both of the viruses that do the most damage to cassava. Choice B states that 'first' and explains why those two viruses matter.

A.why: This choice tells you who developed Kora-7, when, and what cassava is. That's accurate background, but it never says why the variety is important.

C.why: You picked a description of the plant's leaves and roots. Appearance doesn't show significance, so the goal isn't met.

D.why: The notes report resistance in field trials. They don't say crop losses have ended anywhere, let alone across West Africa, so this choice claims more than the notes support.
